issues.body: In the `isinstance(q, dict) and isinstance(gold_count, dict)` branch, validation checks only `answered != gold_count[part]`. It never requires `part` in `gold_keys` or calls `check_entity_gold` with `t["gold_keys"][part]`. For th03, both gold_keys values are entity lists, so either subquery may return arbitrary entities of the expected cardinality and validation succeeds. The new tests mutate same-count entities only for single-query list-gold tasks (th04 and cc04), leaving this dispatch path untested.
issues.fix_hint: After the per-part count check, require a matching `gold_keys` part and, for a non-aggregate subquery with a non-empty entity list, call `check_entity_gold(tid, arm, data, t["gold_keys"][part])`; fail on missing or mismatched part keys. Add an end-to-end mutation test that replaces one th03 entity while preserving that part's row count and asserts `main()` exits non-zero without reporting a gold_count mismatch.
issues.title: Multi-part th03 entity values are still unchecked

verdict.summary: Round 3's major finding remains materially unchanged. The multi-part dispatch for th03 still validates only each part's row count and never compares the returned first-column entities with the corresponding dict-of-lists gold_keys entry. The added end-to-end entity mutations cover th04 and cc04, but not th03. Thus a th03 arm can return an arbitrary same-cardinality entity set for either truth_bearers or info_bearers and pass, contradicting the validator and README claims that multi-part/entity golds are checked. Progress is stagnant because the same major defect remains at the same severity.
